solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Suspect's name associated with signs of debt

parts.note: to dub someone is to give them a name
IOUs are written promises to pay, so tokens of debt

explanation.surface: Someone under suspicion is linked by name to a string of unpaid debts.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition and wordplay. An IOU ('I owe you') is a note acknowledging a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suspect is questionable or of doubtful honesty, a close synonym.

clue.text: Tendency of Democrat to crack

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics
a rift is a crack or split

explanation.surface: A politician seems inclined to break open or fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The drift of something is its general trend or direction, as in the drift of an argument.

clue.text: Police raid damaged most of drug and sports equipment

parts.note: the Bill is British slang for the police

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of the word raid are knocked out of shape and rearranged
most of means the final letter of the drug word is dropped

parts.note: a tablet is a pill of a drug

explanation.surface: Officers bust a drugs den and wreck some gear in a sports hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges RAID into IARD; 'most of' cuts TABLET to TABLE. The Old Bill, or the Bill, is British slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A billiard table is the baize-covered table on which the cue sport of billiards is played.

clue.text: Possessed old women's refuge to the north

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women

indicators.note: in a down clue, going to the north means reading upwards, so the refuge word is turned around

parts.note: a den is a private retreat or refuge

explanation.surface: An old women's shelter up north was once held by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' turns DEN upwards into NED, since in a down entry north is the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessed and owned both mean held as one's property; a straight synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Offence outside public house by mysterious person

indicators.note: outside says the offence word sits around the pub abbreviation

parts.note: a sin is an offence or wrongdoing
PH is the map abbreviation for public house, a British pub
by as in multiplication, 3 by 4, is the times sign X

explanation.surface: Some wrongdoing happens out by a pub, carried out by a shadowy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is read as in multiplication, three by four, which gives the times sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone called a sphinx is enigmatic and inscrutable, after the riddling creature of Greek legend.

clue.text: Around middle of town, salesperson reflected authority

indicators.note: Around means the reflected salesperson wraps about the town's middle letters
reflected, as in a mirror, means the salesperson word is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: middle of takes the centre letters of the word town

explanation.surface: A salesperson in the town centre glimpses officialdom in a shop window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' here takes two letters, since 'town' has an even number of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Power and authority both mean the right or ability to command and control others.

clue.text: Well-liked surgery, regularly full, in standard environment

indicators.note: in signals that the surgery letters go inside another word
an environment surrounds, so the standard word encloses the surgery letters

parts.note: par is the standard or norm, as in golf
an op is a surgical operation

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word full

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of full are taken

explanation.surface: A busy, popular doctor's surgery is described as packed in a normal setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes UL from 'full'; OP and UL then go inside PAR, the standard score.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular means liked or admired by many people, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Forcibly mould creamy confection in fancy teashop

parts.note: a whip is a light dessert made with whipped cream or egg whites
taken as written

indicators.note: fancy here suggests something fanciful or elaborate, telling us to rearrange the letters of teashop

explanation.surface: A café pastry chef presses a creamy dessert into form at a fancy teashop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word placing the confection in the teashop, but it is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: To whip something into shape is an idiom for forcing it into the required condition or form.

clue.text: Invasive plant a gardener withdraws firstly in tall grass

indicators.note: in says the initials sit inside the tall grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing by water

indicators.note: firstly takes the first letter of each of the words a, gardener and withdraws

explanation.surface: A gardener retreats from a weed that has spread among tall grasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragweed is a weed, specifically one known for spreading aggressively and taking over land.

clue.text: Man maybe hoping to include papa, touring archipelago?

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an example of an island

indicators.note: to include means the hoping word takes the papa letter inside it

parts.note: Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man hopes his father will come along on a tour of the islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea, hence 'maybe' signalling an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Island-hopping is travelling from one island to another in a chain, as one would round an archipelago.

clue.text: Right to probe neckwear teacher wore experimentally

indicators.note: to probe means the right letter pushes into the neckwear word

parts.note: a tie is worn around the neck
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A tutor checks whether his tie is properly straight before testing it out.
explanation.definitionFit: To try clothes on is to put them on to see whether they fit, an idiom for a test fitting.

clue.text: See one on European river

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
I is the Roman numeral for one
re means on or about, as in a business letter

explanation.surface: A traveller is told to look at someone standing on a continental river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France, flowing west to the Atlantic.

clue.text: Some cavort, executing whirling motion

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Dancers caper about, performing spinning moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A vortex is a mass of fluid or air spinning around a centre, like a whirlpool.

clue.text: Virginia sits on remarkably clean item of bedding

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another means it comes above, so first

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

indicators.note: remarkably hints at something altered out of the ordinary, so the letters of clean are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman named Virginia perches on a strikingly tidy piece of bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virginia' looks like a woman's name, but it is the US state, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A valance is a short fabric drape around the base of a bed frame, hiding the space beneath.

clue.text: Organ loud — friend set up aural covering

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing
f, forte, is the musical direction for loud

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the friend word is placed upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: An organ plays loudly as a friend sets up some ear protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns PAL into LAP, upwards in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An earflap is a flap on a hat that folds down to protect the ear from cold.

clue.text: Unknown scoundrel and newsman like raunchy film?

parts.note: X is the classic algebraic unknown
a rat is a contemptible, treacherous person
ED is short for editor, a newspaper man

explanation.surface: A shady hack and a nameless villain are mixed up in a seedy film.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows the definition is by example: an X certificate was the old adults-only film rating.
explanation.definitionFit: X-rated describes a film classified as suitable only for adults, typically for sexual content.

clue.text: Times article on centre of Padua, an idyllic place

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: the times or multiplication sign is X
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: centre of takes the letters in the middle of Padua

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on central Padua paints it as a paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it is the multiplication sign X. 'centre of' takes ADU, the middle three letters of PADUA.
explanation.definitionFit: Xanadu, Kubla Khan's summer capital in Coleridge's poem, has become a byword for a place of luxury and beauty.

clue.text: Soapy foam husband removed subsequently

indicators.note: removed means the husband letter is taken away from the foam word

parts.note: lather is the foam made by soap

explanation.surface: A wife washes away the soap suds after her husband has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Later and subsequently both mean at a time after the present or after some event.

clue.text: Helps when relative outwardly tires

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'
sis is short for sister, a relative

indicators.note: outwardly takes only the outer letters of the word tires

explanation.surface: A family member lends a hand when someone starts to flag.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help or aid; both are verbs here in the third person.

clue.text: Expert during square-bashing disheartened military recruit

indicators.note: during says the expert word comes inside the other letters
disheartened removes the heart of square-bashing, leaving just its outer letters

parts.note: a pro is a professional or expert

explanation.surface: An experienced drill instructor discourages a raw young soldier on the parade ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Square-bashing is British slang for military drill on a parade square. A sprog is British slang for a new recruit, or a child.
explanation.definitionFit: In British services slang a sprog is a raw recruit or trainee, a colloquial word for a newcomer.

clue.text: In street, sheltered from wind, rain and snow combined

indicators.note: In means the sheltered word is placed inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the address abbreviation for street
lee is the side sheltered from the wind

explanation.surface: Someone takes shelter in a street from wind and wintry showers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleet is precipitation of partly melted snow or ice mixed with rain.

clue.text: Learn about Lee, new scholarly prize-winner

indicators.note: new tells us the letters are formed into something fresh, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Students are urged to study a fresh biography of a person named Lee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like an anagram signal but is fodder; 'new' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nobel laureate is someone awarded a Nobel Prize, often a distinguished scientist or scholar.

clue.text: Ogle looker perhaps at university

parts.note: an eye is something that looks, a looker
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student eyes up an attractive person on campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looker' usually means an attractive person, but here it is something that looks. Being 'up' is British usage for being in residence at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye up someone is to look at them with obvious desire, which is to ogle.

clue.text: A French gentleman obtains high-class ointment

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: obtains means the gentleman word holds the high-class letter within

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman
U means upper-class, in the old British U and non-U distinction

explanation.surface: A Frenchman of standing gets himself some posh cream.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U was a 1950s British label for upper-class and not upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: An unguent is a soothing salve or cream for skin, the same thing as an ointment.
